subject: Split invoicing, amortization approach & sunset redlines for Brightline
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Le <kevin.le@brightline.com>, Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@brightline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Split invoicing, amortization approach & sunset redlines for Brightline

Kevin / Olivia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per discussion, attaching a clean SOW (SOW_v2.pdf) and the high-level commercial approach we want to confirm before legal redlines:

- Structure: 3-year commitment (annual prepay), with an option to split the first-year invoice into 50% upfront + 50% billed at 6 months for cashflow smoothing.
- Ramp: Year 1 tiered usage (25% / 50% / 25%) with a guaranteed minimum Q1 baseline.
- Early termination: proposed holdback equals the unamortized portion of the term discount; refund delivered as account credit unless otherwise negotiated.
- Sunsetting / co-terming: if BU-level co-terming is requested, true-up prorata across BU contracts; co-terming requests require 60-day notice and may trigger a small admin charge.

Action items: please confirm (1) approval of split invoice cadence, (2) whether you require cash refunds vs credits on termination, and (3) acceptable amortization period for any refundable amount (we typically amortize discounts over the prepaid term).

If this aligns, we’ll prepare redlines and a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: SOW_v2.pdf
From: Kevin Le <kevin.le@brightline.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@brightline.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Split invoicing, amortization approach & sunset redlines for Brightline

Rafael —

Appreciate the recap. A couple quick points from our side:

- Split invoice sounds reasonable, we prefer annual invoicing but can accept the 50/50 split on Y1 as a compromise.
- On early termination: Brightline policy is to prefer cash refunds for material sums; if Redwood requires credits only, we’d need a 12-month amortization schedule and visibility on how credits can be applied across BUs.
- Co-terming: we’d like co-terming across three BUs (Platform, Payments, Analytics). Can Redwood support BU-level allocation of credits / true-ups?

I’ll loop in our legal for redlines if you send a marked-up.

—Kevin
Kevin Le
Head of Procurement, Brightline Systems
kevin.le@brightline.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Split invoicing, amortization approach & sunset redlines for Brightline

Team — forwarding Kevin’s reply. Need legal + finance guidance on two items before we send a formal redline:

1) Cash refunds vs credits: finance prefers credits to avoid cash churn; legal prefers a clean amortization table for any refundable amount.
2) Co-terming across multiple BUs: operations needs an implementation note on how credits will be applied and what metadata we require to keep BU separation.

Aditya: can you draft a simple amortization table (12/24/36 month options) showing the cash vs P&L impact for a $600k prepay?
Kimberly: once we have numbers, can you prepare redline language for: (a) refund mechanism (credit vs cash), (b) early termination calculation, (c) co-terming true-up process?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-08-24T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Split invoicing, amortization approach & sunset redlines for Brightline

Kevin / Olivia —

Thanks — attached are our proposed redlines (redlines_Brightline_0823.docx) with the following commercial revisions based on internal guidance:

- Y1 invoicing: 50% due at execution, remaining 50% billed at month 6. Subsequent years billed annually in advance.
- Refunds: default refund mechanism will be account credits issued within 30 days of termination; we will include an option for a cash refund for refunds > $50k, amortized over 12 months.
- Amortization: term discounts amortize over the prepaid period; for bookkeeping clarity we’ll provide an amortization schedule in the SOW.
- Early termination calculation: refund = remaining prepaid amount - unamortized discount - administrative charge (1% of remaining commit).
- Co-terming: allowed across BUs; credits will be partitioned by BU per the BU identifier provided at execution. Co-term requests require 60 days' notice.

Please confirm these bullets and let us know if Brightline legal will accept the redline doc. If agreed, I’ll ask Legal to issue a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Best,
Rafael

Subject: Final: Amortization threshold and termination language (Brightline)

Hi Olivia / Kevin —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per internal modeling (attached SOW_Final_Brightline_0825.pdf) and finance review:

- Amortization options provided: 12, 24, 36 months. For commercial simplicity we recommend 12-month amortization on refunds > $50k and 36 months for smaller balances; please see table in the attached SOW_Final_Brightline_0825.pdf.
- Cash refund threshold: Redwood will accept cash refunds for amounts > $50k (we can make an exception to your $100k ask for strategic partnership); amounts below will be issued as account credits.
- Early termination fee: remaining prepaid minus amortized discount minus 1% admin charge.
- Co-terming: allowed; credits partitioned by BU identifier provided at contract signature. If Brightline wants unified credits across BUs, we can support that but it will remove the BU-level audit trail and requires an extra compliance step.

If this aligns, we’ll prepare DocuSign (link below) and issue the final envelope next business day.
